# Metric catalogue

Every metric this build can measure: 172 definitions, generated from the `MetricDef` each provider publishes. A scenario selects metrics with its `metrics:` list ([Metrics and outputs](../recording-and-metrics.md#metrics)); each section below says which selection installs its metrics. Visibility `gt` means the metric is computed from ground truth that no node could observe, `node` that a node could compute it from what it received, and `node-and-gt` that it joins both. A health band, where a metric has one, is what `v2xw compare` and the Studio judge a value against.

!!! note "Reading a row"
 *Aggregation* is how observations in a window are reduced. *Min samples* is the count below which a window reports `insufficient` instead of a value. *Does not account for* is what the definition deliberately leaves out.

### `acceleration` { #m-acceleration }

The distribution of sampled actor accelerations over the window.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | m/s² |
| Aggregation | distribution |
| Visibility | gt |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): traffic and safety metrics (code) |

Does not account for:

- the same time-weighting bias as `speed`
- jerk, which the kinematics channel does not carry

### `air_bytes_per_payload_byte` { #m-air-bytes-per-payload-byte }

Octets on the air per octet of application payload: how many bytes the air carries for each byte the application wanted to send.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | B/B |
| Aggregation | ratio: Σ octets on the air / Σ application payload octets |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t`, `msg_type` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): the frame's layers and their sizes (code) |

Does not account for:

- frames with no payload/envelope split
- the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time

### `airtime_per_node` { #m-airtime-per-node }

Transmitted air time per node, divided by the window's length. With no dimension, the mean over the nodes that transmitted in the window.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ms/s |
| Aggregation | rate |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t`, `node` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): radio and network metric catalog (code) |
| Better | lower (standard basis) |
| Healthy | within the 1 % duty cycle the relaxed DCC state allows |
| Caution | 10.0: above 10 ms/s: more than the relaxed DCC state's 1 % duty cycle |
| Unhealthy | 30.0: above 30 ms/s: past the 3 % per-station duty-cycle ceiling |
| Band source | ETSI TS 102 687 V1.2.1 reactive DCC Relaxed state (T_on 1 ms per T_off 100 ms, 1 %); EN 302 571 / TS 102 687 adaptive δ_max 0.03 (3 % = 30 ms/s) |

Does not account for:

- receive-side occupancy
- inter-frame spacing and backoff, which are not transmitted time

### `aoi` { #m-aoi }

Age of information: how old, on average over time, the freshest message a receiver holds from each neighbour is — over the vehicles truly within 100 m that it has heard (SAE J2945/1's vPERRange; Kaul et al.'s system age), integrated exactly between mobility steps over the pairs within range at each step. Broken down at 100 m and 300 m, and `all`: every link's sawtooth but a VRU device's, integrated exactly between its deliveries, whatever the distance, which far links that rarely deliver dominate. Vehicles only: pedestrians' and riders' devices beacon at their own, lower rates, so vehicles' age about them within 100 m is the class `vru` sample.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ms |
| Aggregation | ratio: Σ age × time / Σ time |
| Visibility | node-and-gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `radius`, `class` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | Kaul, Gruteser, Rai, Kenney, IEEE SECON 2011; Kaul, Yates, Gruteser, IEEE INFOCOM 2012 (paper) |
| Better | lower (standard basis) |
| Healthy | what receivers know is under three message intervals old |
| Caution | 300.0: above 300 ms: receivers' picture is three or more 10 Hz intervals old |
| Unhealthy | 600.0: above 600 ms: older than the longest gap J2945/1 congestion control allows |
| Band source | SAE J2945/1 10 Hz BSM and vMaxITT 600 ms (Ahmad et al., IEEE TVT 68(3) 2019, Table I); three intervals is the run analyst's stale threshold |

Does not account for:

- neighbours in range never heard, or unheard for over aoi_restart_s: nar counts them
- pseudonym changes: links are keyed by the true sender

### `aoi_peak` { #m-aoi-peak }

Peak age of information: the age of a receiver's information about a sender just before a new message from it arrives.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ms |
| Aggregation | distribution |
| Visibility | node-and-gt |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | Costa, Codreanu, Ephremides, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 62(4), 2016 (paper) |

Does not account for:

- the first message on a link, which has no predecessor
- links restarted after a silence longer than aoi_restart_s
- links farther than 100 m at the delivery

| Field | Value |
|---|---|

| Aggregation | rate |

| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): bytes per accounting bucket (code) |

### `bytes_per_vehicle_hour` { #m-bytes-per-vehicle-hour }

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | B/(veh·h) |
| Aggregation | ratio: octets in the bucket / equipped-vehicle hours |
| Visibility | node-and-gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `bucket` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): invariant I-N1: every byte in exactly one bucket (code) |

- roadside units' own time, which is not vehicle time
- a vehicle's first record, which contributes no time

| Min samples | 1 |

Does not account for:

- whether anyone received them
- spatial reuse: this is a network total, not one channel's load

### `cbr` { #m-cbr }

Channel busy ratio as measured by the MAC: for 802.11p, the fraction of a 100 ms window with CCA busy above −85 dBm; for C-V2X, the TS 38.215 §5.1.27 / TS 36.214 definition. Reported as a distribution over the window's per-node measurements; each is a node's own measurement over its own window, so the distribution is reported whatever the node count, with that count.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | distribution |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t`, `channel` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | 3GPP TS 38.215 §5.1.27; TS 36.214 (standard) |
| Better | lower (standard basis) |
| Healthy | below 0.50: congestion control has nothing to do |
| Caution | 0.5: above 0.50: SAE J2945/1 congestion control is lowering power and message rate |
| Unhealthy | 0.68: above the 0.68 ETSI congestion target; vehicles will throttle their messages |
| Band source | ETSI TS 102 687 V1.2.1 §5.4 (adaptive DCC CBR_target 0.68); SAE J2945/1 vMinCBP 50 % (Ahmad et al., IEEE TVT 68(3) 2019, Table I) |

Does not account for:

- energy the receiver could not hear (a hidden terminal)
- which node measured it: this is the distribution across nodes

### `cert_bytes_share` { #m-cert-bytes-share }

|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: Σ attached-certificate octets / Σ envelope octets |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t`, `msg_type` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): the frame's layers and their sizes (code) |

Does not account for:

- peer-to-peer certificate responses outside ordinary messages
- the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time

### `channel_load` { #m-channel-load }

Offered load against capacity, as each node sees it: the air time of every frame arriving above the −85 dBm busy threshold plus the node's own offered air time, over the window. One is a channel exactly full; above one, more is being offered than the channel can carry.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | distribution |
| Visibility | node-and-gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `node` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | Torrent-Moreno, Mittag, Santi, Hartenstein, IEEE Trans. Veh. Technol. 58(7), 2009 (paper) |
| Better | lower (standard basis) |
| Healthy | below 0.50: congestion control has nothing to do |
| Caution | 0.5: above 0.50: SAE J2945/1 congestion control is lowering power and message rate |
| Unhealthy | 0.68: above the 0.68 ETSI congestion target; vehicles will throttle their messages |
| Band source | ETSI TS 102 687 V1.2.1 §5.4 (adaptive DCC CBR_target 0.68); SAE J2945/1 vMinCBP 50 % (Ahmad et al., IEEE TVT 68(3) 2019, Table I) |

Does not account for:

- frames neighbours' MACs refused, which never reached the air
- the merging of overlaps: overlapping frames are summed

| Min samples | 1 |

### `loss_rate` { #m-loss-rate }

The fraction of all resolved reception attempts that were lost to one cause — a PHY cause (collision, half-duplex, below-sensitivity, fading, …) or one above it (verification overflow, invalid signature, revoked, …). Summed over causes it is one minus the delivery ratio.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: attempts lost with this cause / attempts resolved |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t`, `cause` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): radio and network metric catalog (code) |

Does not account for:

- attempts still in flight when the run ended
- receivers outside the engine's candidate range

### `mac_access_delay` { #m-mac-access-delay }

Channel-access delay per transmitted frame: from the frame reaching the MAC (its signature complete) to its preamble going on the air — AIFS, backoff and deferral to a busy medium.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ms |
| Aggregation | distribution |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | IEEE 802.11-2020 §10.23.2 (standard) |
| Better | lower (engineering basis) |
| Healthy | p95 channel access within 10 ms |
| Caution | 10.0: p95 channel access above 10 ms: a tenth of the 100 ms safety budget |
| Unhealthy | 20.0: p95 channel access above 20 ms: a fifth of the 100 ms safety budget is spent waiting for the channel |
| Band source | engineering choice against the 100 ms budget of 3GPP TS 22.185 §5.1: 20 % is the run analyst's access_budget_fraction |

Does not account for:

- frames the MAC refused, which never got access
- signing, which happens before the MAC has the frame

### `mac_drops` { #m-mac-drops }

Frames the MAC refused in the window: a full access-category queue or a frame over the MSDU cap.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | count |
| Aggregation | count |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | IEEE 802.11-2020 §10.23.2 (standard) |

Does not account for:

- frames the node itself never generated because DCC held it back

### `mac_queue_depth` { #m-mac-queue-depth }

Frames waiting in a node's EDCA access-category queues, at each MAC report, across nodes.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | count |
| Aggregation | distribution |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | IEEE 802.11-2020 §10.23.2 (standard) |
| Better | lower (engineering basis) |
| Healthy | the transmit queue is usually empty |
| Caution | 1.0: the transmit queue is rarely empty: frames wait behind each other |
| Unhealthy | 5.0: the transmit queue is backing up; frames will be stale or dropped |
| Band source | engineering choice: a mean depth above one frame is a queue that is rarely empty (the run analyst's queue_depth_saturated); five frames is half a second of 10 Hz messages |

Does not account for:

- the depth between reports: it is sampled, not time-averaged
- frames still in the node's signer, which have not reached the MAC

### `mean_speed` { #m-mean-speed }

The **space**-mean speed, `q / k` — not the time-mean speed, which is 6–12 % higher on a mixed-speed signalised dataset (Wardrop 1952).

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | m/s |
| Aggregation | mean |
| Visibility | gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `region` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | L. C. Edie 1963; FHWA Traffic Flow Theory ch. 2 (paper) |

Does not account for:

- lanes whose length the run did not declare
- the time-mean speed, which is a different quantity

### `nar` { #m-nar }

Neighbourhood awareness ratio: of the vehicles truly within R metres of each equipped vehicle, the fraction it has received a message from in the last second. Pedestrians' and riders' devices are neither receivers nor neighbours: they beacon at their own rates. Reported at R = 100 m and R = 300 m. Sampled at every mobility step and pooled over the window; the 95 % Wilson interval is computed on the number of distinct neighbour pairs, not on the samples, because one pair seen ten times is not ten independent observations — so a sparse run reports an estimate with a wide interval instead of refusing.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: neighbours within R heard within T / neighbours within R |
| Visibility | node-and-gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `radius` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | Boban and d'Orey, IEEE Trans. Veh. Technol. 65(6), 2016; the interval: Brown, Cai, DasGupta, Statistical Science 16(2), 2001 (Wilson for small n) and Kish, Survey Sampling, 1965 (effective sample size of a clustered sample) (paper) |
| Better | higher (engineering basis) |
| Healthy | vehicles know about at least 95 % of their neighbours within 100 m |
| Caution | 0.95: awareness of neighbours within 100 m below 95 % |
| Unhealthy | 0.9: vehicles are unaware of more than 1 in 10 neighbours within 100 m |
| Band source | engineering choice matching the 0.9 reception level of 3GPP TR 37.885 (the run analyst's awareness_floor) |

Does not account for:

- roadside units, which have no ground-truth kinematics
- whether the neighbour was reachable at all (it is counted either way)

### `net_header_overhead` { #m-net-header-overhead }

The share of the octets on the air that are the network and transport header: WSMP for the US stack, GeoNetworking plus BTP for the European one.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: Σ network and transport header octets / Σ octets on the air |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t`, `msg_type` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): the frame's layers and their sizes (code) |

Does not account for:

- the LLC/SNAP octets, which are in link_overhead
- the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time

### `offered_load` { #m-offered-load }

PSDU bits every node handed to its MAC in the window, whatever became of them, per second — network-wide.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | bit/s |
| Aggregation | rate |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): radio and network metric catalog (code) |

Does not account for:

- the PHY preamble and tail, which are air time and not bits
- spatial reuse: this is a network total, not one channel's load

### `p2pcd_requests` { #m-p2pcd-requests }

Peer-to-peer certificate distribution requests per second, all nodes: signed SPDUs carrying a learning request for a certificate the sender could not resolve, out-of-band (p2pcdLearningRequest) or inline (inlineP2pcdRequest), IEEE 1609.2-2022 clause 8. Before 2026-10-25 this name counted digest misses, which are now `digest_misses`.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | 1/s |
| Aggregation | rate |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): security processing metrics (code) |

Does not account for:

- the responses and the certificates learned
- nodes whose P2PCD entity is off, which send none

### `pdr` { #m-pdr }

Packet reception ratio (3GPP TR 36.885 §A.2.1.4): of the equipped receivers truly within range of each frame, the fraction that decoded it. The headline is within 300 m; `pdr[100m]` and `pdr[300m]` are the two ranges and `dist_bin` the 20 m curve. Every receiver in range counts, whether or not the radio evaluated a link to it, so the figure does not depend on the engine's candidate range.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: receivers within range that decoded the frame / receivers within range |
| Visibility | gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `radius`, `dist_bin` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | 3GPP TR 36.885 §A.2.1.4: the packet reception ratio of one transmitted packet is X/Y, Y the receivers located in the distance range (a, b) from the transmitter and X those among them that received it; evaluated in 20 m bins (standard) |
| Better | higher (standard basis) |
| Healthy | at least 95 % of receivers within 100 m decode each message |
| Caution | 0.95: below 95 % within 100 m: losses at short range, where a link should be clean |
| Unhealthy | 0.9: below 90 % within 100 m: under the reliability V2V evaluations require |
| Band source | 3GPP TR 37.885 (V2X evaluation methodology reads range at a 0.9 packet reception ratio); 0.95 within near range is the run analyst's engineering choice |

Does not account for:

- receivers beyond the stated range
- reception above the PHY: a decoded frame the receiver then dropped or could not verify counts as received here (delivery_ratio is the application-level figure)
- coverage: a transmitter with no receiver within range contributes no trials

### `pdr_all_pairs` { #m-pdr-all-pairs }

Received frames divided by every reception the engine evaluated: every pair within its candidate range, however far and whatever stands between them, per 25 m distance bin. Not the literature's delivery ratio — its denominator is set by the engine's candidate range, so pairs behind a building a kilometre apart count as trials. Kept to show what the radio was asked to do; `pdr` is the figure to quote.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: received frames / evaluated receptions |
| Visibility | node-and-gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `dist_bin` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): radio and network metric catalog (code) |

Does not account for:

- receivers outside the engine's candidate range
- coverage: a transmitter with no candidate receivers contributes no trials

### `pdr_by_cause` { #m-pdr-by-cause }

The share of losses attributable to each loss cause. Invariant I-R3 requires every loss to carry exactly one cause, so the shares sum to one by construction — and when they do not, that is an I-R3violation and not a rounding artefact.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: losses with this cause / all losses |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t`, `cause` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): radio and network metric catalog (code) |

Does not account for:

- a frame lost for two reasons at once
- losses the producer recorded without a cause

| Field | Value |

### `pir` { #m-pir }

Packet inter-reception time: the gap between successive receptions from the same transmitter at the same receiver. Pedestrians' and riders' devices, which beacon at their own lower rates, are the class `vru` sample rather than the headline.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | s |
| Aggregation | distribution |
| Visibility | node-and-gt |
| Dimensions | `t`, `class` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 30 |
| Source | Martelli, Elena Renda, Resta, Santi, 'A measurement-based study of beaconing performance in IEEE 802.11p vehicular networks', IEEE INFOCOM 2012 (packet inter-reception time) (paper) |
| Better | lower (standard basis) |
| Healthy | p95 gap between messages from one sender under 0.3 s |
| Caution | 0.3: p95 gap above 0.3 s: three or more 10 Hz messages lost in a row |
| Unhealthy | 0.6: p95 gap above 0.6 s: longer than J2945/1 ever schedules; messages are lost |

Does not account for:

Time to collision for a closing same-lane pair: `gap / (v_follower − v_leader)`, sampled at every mobility step. Reported as a distribution; the minimum of the run is its `min`.

## Credential and privacy metrics (`all`, security path) { #s-all-on-a-run-with-a-security-path }

Installed by `metrics: [all]` (or by name) when the run has a security path: a backend or security protocol, roadside units, attackers or local detectors.

| Metric | Unit | Aggregation | Visibility | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`backend_link_up`](#m-backend-link-up) | ratio | ratio: vehicle security rows with a usable backend link / vehicle security rows | node | The share of vehicles whose backend access (cellular coverage, a relaying roadside unit in range) was usable, over the window |
| [`cert_pool_valid`](#m-cert-pool-valid) | count | distribution | node | Certificates each vehicle holds valid at the instant of its security row |
| [`linkability`](#m-linkability) | ratio | ratio: pseudonym changes a passive observer linked correctly / pseudonym changes | gt | The share of pseudonym changes a global passive observer bridges correctly, cumulative over the run |
| [`pseudonym_change_rate`](#m-pseudonym-change-rate) | 1/(veh·h) | mean | node | Pseudonym changes per vehicle-hour: all changes over all vehicle-time observed |

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | ratio |
| Aggregation | ratio: pseudonym changes a passive observer linked correctly / pseudonym changes |
| Visibility | gt |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 1e-06 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): privacy metrics: pseudonym change rate and linkability (code) |
| Better | lower (engineering basis) |
| Healthy | an observer links few pseudonym changes |
| Caution | 0.2: an observer links more than 1 in 5 pseudonym changes |
| Unhealthy | 0.5: an observer links most pseudonym changes: pseudonyms are not protecting vehicles |
| Band source | engineering choice; 0.5 is the run analyst's linkability threshold |

Does not account for:

- an observer with less than full coverage

### `pseudonym_change_rate` { #m-pseudonym-change-rate }

Pseudonym changes per vehicle-hour: all changes over all vehicle-time observed.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | 1/(veh·h) |
| Aggregation | mean |
| Visibility | node |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.0001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): privacy metrics: pseudonym change rate and linkability (code) |

Does not account for:

- changes before a vehicle's first security row

## Signing overhead (`signing`) { #s-signing }

Opt-in: `metrics: [all, signing]`, or any `sig_*` name. Not part of a bare `all`.

| Metric | Unit | Aggregation | Visibility | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`sig_backend_bytes`](#m-sig-backend-bytes) | B/s | rate | public | Credential-system octets to and from devices per second: certificate provisioning, downloads and the requests for them |
| [`sig_ca_busy`](#m-sig-ca-busy) | ms/s | rate | public | Certificate-authority service time per second of simulated time: what the scheme costs the backend |
| [`sig_ca_sign_rate`](#m-sig-ca-sign-rate) | 1/s | rate | public | Signatures the certificate authorities made per second |
| [`sig_cbr_extra`](#m-sig-cbr-extra) | ratio | ratio: mean CBR × security octet share / 1 | node | Estimated channel busy ratio the security envelope adds: the measured CBR times the envelope's share of the octets on the air |
| [`sig_cert_airtime_share`](#m-sig-cert-airtime-share) | ratio | ratio: Σ certificate octets / Σ octets on the air | node | The share of the octets on the air that are attached certificates |
| [`sig_cert_bytes`](#m-sig-cert-bytes) | B/msg | ratio: Σ attached-certificate octets / signed messages | node | Attached-certificate octets per signed message, averaged over messages with and without one |
| [`sig_e2e_added`](#m-sig-e2e-added) | ms | distribution | node | End-to-end latency added by security on a delivered message: the wait for and time of signing, plus the wait for and time of verification |
| [`sig_e2e_added_share`](#m-sig-e2e-added-share) | ratio | ratio: Σ latency added by security / Σ end-to-end latency | node | The share of end-to-end latency that is signing and verification |
| [`sig_fragmented_share`](#m-sig-fragmented-share) | ratio | ratio: messages in more than one frame / messages sent | node | The share of messages that had to be fragmented, which large signatures cause |
| [`sig_fragments_per_msg`](#m-sig-fragments-per-msg) | frames/msg | ratio: frames on the air / messages sent | node | Fragments on the air per message: 1 when every signed message fits the MTU |
| [`sig_neighbour_capacity`](#m-sig-neighbour-capacity) | count | mean | node | How many neighbours a device can verify every message from before its queue grows: verification capacity over each sender's message rate |
| [`sig_reassembly_loss`](#m-sig-reassembly-loss) | ratio | ratio: fragmented SDUs failed or expired / fragmented SDUs resolved | node | Fragmented messages a receiver could not reassemble: the delivery lost to fragmentation |
| [`sig_security_airtime_share`](#m-sig-security-airtime-share) | ratio | ratio: Σ envelope octets / Σ octets on the air | node | The share of the octets on the air that are the security envelope — headers, signer identifier and signature — with certificates |

## Traffic control (`traffic`) { #s-traffic }

Installed with a `traffic:` section, or with `metrics: [all, traffic]` or one of these names.

| Metric | Unit | Aggregation | Visibility | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`signal_gap_outs`](#m-signal-gap-outs) | count | count | public | Actuated greens ended early because no vehicle reached the detectors within the passage time while another approach waited |
| [`signal_max_outs`](#m-signal-max-outs) | count | count | public | Actuated greens ended at their maximum while vehicles were still arriving |
| [`traffic_jammed`](#m-traffic-jammed) | count | count | public | Vehicles that stood still for the whole gridlock timeout: each one is a jam the network did not clear by itself |
| [`traffic_removed`](#m-traffic-removed) | count | count | public | Vehicles the gridlock resolution removed, because no lane on the rest of their route had room |
| [`traffic_teleports`](#m-traffic-teleports) | count | count | public | Vehicles the gridlock resolution moved on along their route, as SUMO's teleport does |

### `traffic_teleports` { #m-traffic-teleports }

Vehicles the gridlock resolution moved on along their route, as SUMO's teleport does.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | count |
| Aggregation | count |
| Visibility | public |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): v2xw_engine::actuated (traffic.control) (code) |
| Better | lower (engineering basis) |
| Healthy | no vehicle was stuck long enough to be moved on |
| Caution | 0.0: a few vehicles were stuck past the gridlock timeout: look for a blocked junction |
| Unhealthy | 10.0: more than 10 vehicles were stuck past the gridlock timeout: the demand is more than this network carries, or the network has a fault |
| Band source | engineering choice: SUMO warns of every teleport; a calibrated run should have none |

Does not account for:

- a jam shorter than the gridlock timeout, and a vehicle the timeout is off for (0 s); a pedestrian's signal call, which the detectors do not see

### `ssm_collisions` { #m-ssm-collisions }

Encounters whose bodies overlapped (SUMO code 111), logged when the encounter closed.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | count |
| Aggregation | count |
| Visibility | gt |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | SUMO documentation, Simulation/Output/SSM Device (thresholds TTC 3.0 s, DRAC 3.0, MDRAC 3.4, PPET 2.0 s, range 50 m, extratime 5 s); Gettman et al. 2008, FHWA-HRT-08-051 (SSAM); Laureshyn et al. 2010; Fazekas et al. 2017 (paper) |

Does not account for:

- an encounter still open at the run's last window
- a turning vehicle's curved path: extrapolation is straight

## Runtime diagnostics (library only) { #s-runtime }

Defined in `v2xw_metrics::runtime` and installed by `v2xw_metrics::register_all`, but **not installed in an engine run**: the engine reads no clock. Diagnostic, excluded from every digest.

| Metric | Unit | Aggregation | Visibility | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`events_per_second`](#m-events-per-second) | 1/s | rate | meta | Events processed per wall-clock second |
| [`events_processed`](#m-events-processed) | count | count | meta | Events delivered to this provider |
| [`memory_high_water_mark`](#m-memory-high-water-mark) | B | max | meta | The peak resident size the host reported during the run |
| [`wall_clock_per_sim_second`](#m-wall-clock-per-sim-second) | s/s | rate | meta | Wall-clock seconds per simulated second — the run's slowdown factor |

### `events_per_second` { #m-events-per-second }

Events processed per wall-clock second. **A diagnostic**: machine-dependent, and excluded from every digested artefact.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | 1/s |
| Aggregation | rate |
| Visibility | meta |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): runtime diagnostics (code) |
| Diagnostic | yes: machine-dependent, excluded from digests |

Does not account for:

- the machine it ran on, which dominates it
- what else the machine was doing

### `events_processed` { #m-events-processed }

Events delivered to this provider. A property of the run, **not** of the machine, so it is digested: two hosts that processed different numbers of events did not run the same simulation.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | count |
| Aggregation | count |
| Visibility | meta |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): runtime diagnostics (code) |

Does not account for:

- channels this provider was not told to count
- events the engine produced and the recorder dropped

### `memory_high_water_mark` { #m-memory-high-water-mark }

The peak resident size the host reported during the run. **A diagnostic**: machine-dependent, and excluded from every digested artefact.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | B |
| Aggregation | max |
| Visibility | meta |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): runtime diagnostics (code) |
| Diagnostic | yes: machine-dependent, excluded from digests |

Does not account for:

- the allocator, the page size and the platform's accounting
- the engine's own byte counts, which are deterministic

### `wall_clock_per_sim_second` { #m-wall-clock-per-sim-second }

Wall-clock seconds per simulated second — the run's slowdown factor. **A diagnostic**: machine-dependent, and excluded from every digested artefact.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Unit | s/s |
| Aggregation | rate |
| Visibility | meta |
| Dimensions | `t` |
| Grid (quantum) | 0.001 |
| Min samples | 1 |
| Source | assumption (this engine's own definition, no external source): runtime diagnostics (code) |
| Diagnostic | yes: machine-dependent, excluded from digests |

Does not account for:

- the machine, the thread count and the tier planner's choices
- time-dilation windows, which change what a simulated second costs
